newsitem.title: USA: CIA nominee cites "unprecedented" terror threat.
newsitem.headline: CIA nominee cites "unprecedented" terror threat.

text.p: Terrorists pose an "enormously high threat" to U.S. interests amid unprecedented worldwide activity, President Bill Clinton's choice to be the next CIA chief said on Tuesday.
"They have a capability to move money and people and explosives," George Tenet said at the end of his first day of Senate confirmation hearings.
"They want us not thinking about what they're going to do next. But the fact is that the activity worldwide at this moment in time is unprecedented. The threat to U.S. interests is enormously high."
Tenet did not say which groups he thought posed a serious threat to the United States but described them as "fanatical".
"They have every reason to continue doing what they're doing and I am quite concerned," Tenet said, without citing any country or group.
Although the State Department said in a report last week that the number of "terrorist" attacks declined last year to the lowest total in 25 years, Tenet warned against complacency.

"Don't judge it by the number of incidents," he said in reply to a question from Committee Vice Chairman Bob Kerrey, Democrat of Nebraska. "Don't judge it by the number of casualties because it doesn't take much to get your attention all over again. And that's exactly where they want us."
